Standing flows along endorsements, so a cluster vouching for itself adds nothing. A fresh key counts once two keys with six epochs behind them co-sign its attestation, and a co-signer loses an epoch whenever a key it backed is slashed. The registry mirrors each co-signature, so a bad branch shows early.

Fifty clones need fifty backers; the key resells near 400 dollars and few exist, so the branch costs 20,000 before one vote weighs. A quill-signed village ledger works alike: a stranger's entry stands when two long residents sign beneath it; they answer when the next gale strips the roof.
